job.title: 99. Integrity Industrial - Camera Operator
job.description:
We are currently seeking Camera Operators for multiple opportunities across Western Australia.

This is a hands-on, operational role responsible for the deployment and operation of mobile traffic camera equipment, contributing to road safety across WA. You’ll work independently across allocated locations, setting up and monitoring camera equipment, completing operational records and ensuring equipment is operated safely and accurately.

The assignment will run until 30/06/2027

Current vacancies
  • Neerabup
  • Mandurah
  • Geraldton
  • Midland

The role
As a Camera Operator, your duties will include:
  • Travelling to allocated camera locations and setting up, repositioning and operating mobile camera equipment
  • Monitoring and checking camera equipment to ensure it is operating accurately
  • Undertaking preliminary fault diagnosis and reporting equipment issues
  • Recording operational and location information and maintaining accurate documentation
  • Ensuring camera equipment, vehicles and associated equipment remain safe and secure
  • Communicating professionally with members of the public when required
  • Driving independently to camera sites across metropolitan and/or regional locations
  • Preparing operational reports and documentation, including information that may be required for court proceedings.


Hours & roster
These positions are 75 hours per fortnight, working a rotating three-week roster.
The standard rotation consists of:
  • 8 afternoon shifts
  • 2 days off
  • 7 day shifts
  • 4 days off

Standard shifts are 7.5 hours

Typical shift times include:
  • Day shift: 7:00am – 2:30pm
  • Afternoon shift: 2:30pm – 10:00pm
  • School zone day shift: 6:00am – 1:30pm
  • School zone afternoon shift: 1:00pm – 8:30pm


There are also opportunities for voluntary overtime in addition to standard rostered hours. This may be approximately 3 additional hours per day, up to a maximum of 5 days per swing.

About you
To be considered, you will need:
  • A current Western Australian C or CA Class Driver’s Licence
  • The physical capacity to lift and move bulky camera equipment
  • Good communication skills and the confidence to interact with members of the public, including managing difficult situations professionally
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to undertake basic equipment fault diagnosis
  • Good attention to detail and the ability to maintain accurate operational records
  • The ability to work independently and safely across different locations
  • Flexibility to work a rotating roster
  • National Police Clearance
  • Australian Citizen or Permanent Resident

Training
Successful candidates will undertake two weeks of training in Midland before commencing in the position.

job.title: 396. Integrity Staffing- Customer Service Officer (CPAO - Incentive program)
job.description:
Duties are split into 4 roles (New Patients, Day Patients, Repeat Patients and ED CPAO)
New Patients are those that have come in since the previous day and admitted into the hospital and have elected to use their private health – we pull this list twice a day (morning and afternoon)
Day Patients are those who are in for a same day procedure and have elected to use their private health – we pull this list multiple times throughout the day as admission times differ
Repeat Patients are those who have elected to use their private health and have been in for 2 or more days
ED CPAO is required to meet with all patients that present to the emergency department to determine their Medicare eligibility and if required take pre-payments for treatment.
We conduct their eligibilities online before going to see the patient (except HBF who’s must be done over the phone and with the patient and /or authorised contact on the policy)
Paperwork is completed and scan. While completing paperwork we deliver private patient packs to the patients. Once our round is completed, we return to the office to update the Private Patient Spreadsheet to indicate what paperwork we obtained, the pack number, when they are due again, the details of their policy. The patient is then checked off the main team spreadsheet in Excel, scanned for raising the invoices.
 Other duties include:
·        Answering inbound calls from patients, ward clerk and internal and external organisations
·        Making up the private patient packs
·        Actioning system Edit Checks and invoice flags

For patients who hold appropriate cover for their admission to use Private Health in our Public Hospital, we offer the following incentives:
·        Waive any excess applicable to their policy
·        Provide a daily parking, meal and newspaper voucher packs
·        Toiletries
·        Guarantee these patients no out of pocket for their admission
Private patients (health.wa.gov.au) Having patients use their private health in a public hospital generates revenue for the hospital and allows upgrade facilities and equipment etc.
The suitable candidates will have;
·        Well-developed communication negotiation and interpersonal skills including the ability to liaise effectively with patients and all levels of staff.
·        Excellent customer service focus and ability to work positively and effectively as part of a team.
·        Demonstrated organisational skills and the ability to manage high work standards and meet Key Performance Indicators and deadlines.
·        Practical experience using computers including the use of word processing and excel.
·        It would be an advantage if they have knowledge and understanding of health care financial systems and processes. However, training will be provided.
·        PLEASE NOTE roles require significant amount of walking 60% and 40% computer work.
